rationale: Both confirmed findings were about the same implementation object that the v1 map never named: the instance's in-memory log watermark (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm together with lastSnapshotIndex/lastSnapshotTerm), which backs getLastLog/getLastEntry/getLastIndex, the AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog a follower returns, the previous-log comparison and the last-log coordinate a candidate advertises. This handoff adds that Fact and makes its actual validity condition - it must describe the log and snapshot the instance really holds - explicit, including the two runtime transitions that violate it. b-append-entries gains the missing produce/consume edges to the Fact because it is the handler that raises and truncates the log part and reads it back for the previous-log check.

feedback.answered: Two implementation responsibilities are now confirmed in scope against fixed artifacts executed by the runner. First, after appendEntries has deleted a conflicting suffix and the following StoreLogs of the replacement entries fails, the follower's log watermark still counts the deleted indices while its durable log no longer holds them (raft.go 1524-1544; artifact 25473e1b731e4c2692e47975fef6d3a0, executed as de1a5dd120d44cfa887ed4a83c31c01a: raft_last_log_index 3 against store last index 2, reported_success false). Second, after installSnapshot successfully restores a snapshot and clears a monotonic log store, the follower's watermark keeps the pre-install index instead of the installed snapshot index (raft.go 1814-1955, no setLastLog anywhere in the handler; artifact 58ebdb2f92184614b01ecfab56fe2bc9, executed as af5ed6e5cd714a38bc74fced5d1bbcc5: raft_last_log_index 10 against store last index 0 and snapshot index 4). Both are the same implementation object, which the v1 map did not name; this submission adds Fact F-log-watermark with its real validity condition and links b-append-entries to it.
remaining: Reachability from a legal leader history of the installSnapshot case (a follower whose watermark index exceeds the leader's snapshot index) is still open, as is whether the leader's next AppendEntries raises nextIndex again from the stale reported value.

For the truncation-failure case the leader-side recovery is still unexercised: whether nextIndex walks down to a point where the follower can accept, or the follower stays unrepaired short of a restart, remains unknown, as does whether a later request could drive processLogs into the missing range.

The non-monotonic compaction branch of installSnapshot (TrailingLogs leaving the removed entries in place) and the shouldSnapshot delta computed from the log store's LastIndex minus the snapshot index were read but not investigated.
The explained rollback Candidate's unit-claim-config-rollback-consistency is still registered as pending work.
feedback.rationale: The added Fact states the assertion actually established (what the watermark means, when it is valid, that it is in-memory and rebuilt only at construction) rather than the two failures, which are recorded as the open boundaries of that validity condition and are already retained as confirmed check results. The map change is a dependency clarification for b-append-entries, not a semantic revision, and it preserves every existing proposition and the basis of both confirmed artifacts.

b-append-entries.rationale: appendEntries raises the log part of the watermark when it stores new entries (setLastLog after a successful StoreLogs), replaces it when it truncates a conflicting suffix, and reads it back for the previous-log coordinate and for the LastLog it reports. The v1 behavior described the log-entry and commit consequences of that handler but had no edge to the watermark Fact, so its reads and writes of lastLog/lastLogIdx were unrepresented.
b-append-entries.preserves: Adding the produce/consume edges changes no existing proposition, premise or observation: the handler's owner, trigger, guards, effects and branches are untouched, its existing F-log-entry and F-commit-index edges are unchanged, and both confirmed checks remain valid against the same bound lines (raft.go 1524-1543 and the install path they reference) and the same execution records. The new edges only record the third fact this handler already establishes and consumes.
